:::{#def-euclidean-norm}
#### Euclidean norm

The **Euclidean norm** (or *length*) of a vector $\vx$ of length $p$ is

$$\norm{\vx} \eqdef \sqrt{\vx \cdot \vx} = \sqrt{\sumip x_i^2}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-euclidean-norm}
#### The length of a vector

For $\vx = (3, 4)$:

$$
\ba
\norm{\vx}
&= \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2}
&& \text{(definition of the norm)}
\\
&= \sqrt{25}
&& \text{(square and add)}
\\
&= 5
\ea
$$

The vector $(0.6, 0.8)$ has norm $\sqrt{0.36 + 0.64} = 1$.

:::
